args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After the deploy of checkout-api v2.3.1 to production, health checks failed in all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west). The service was unhealthy with an error rate of about 18%. The staging build v2.3.1-rc was also marked unhealthy. checkout-api was rolled back in all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback, all regions run v2.3.0, the service is healthy, and the error rate is about 0.2%. Follow-up: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure before redeploying it, and find out why it was promoted when its staging build was unhealthy.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions and it's healthy again. Opening the SEV2 incident went wrong, though: there are now two identical incidents, and on-call has been paged twice.

**Rollback:**
- v2.3.1 was failing health checks in us-east, us-west and eu-west, with an error rate of about 18%. Its staging build (v2.3.1-rc) had also been marked unhealthy.
- v2.3.0 was the most recent release that was healthy in production. It had been healthy before, so this didn't need change-manager approval.
- I checked after the rollback: all three regions are on v2.3.0, the service is healthy and the error rate is about 0.2%.

**Incident:**
- My first attempt to open the SEV2 timed out. I checked the incident list right away and it was empty, so I opened it again. That created INC-0002.
- When I checked again, the first attempt had gone through after all, as INC-0001. Both incidents have the same title and summary: what failed, the rollback, how I confirmed it, and follow-ups (find the root cause, and find out why v2.3.1 was promoted when its staging build was unhealthy).
- I can't close or merge incidents with the tools I have. Someone needs to close INC-0002 as a duplicate of INC-0001 and let on-call know the second page was the same issue.
